newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech CEZ mulls new target for N-plant completion.
newsitem.headline: Czech CEZ mulls new target for N-plant completion.

text.p: The completion of a nuclear power plant at Temelin will be four to 13 months later than its last target date of September 1997, a spokesman for the plant's owner CEZ a.s. said on Tuesday.
Spokesman Ladislav Kriz said an exact new deadline will be known by the end of this year after CEZ concludes talks with with the plant's general contractor, engineering group Skoda Praha a.s.
CEZ has delayed the completion several times, the latest because of rewiring of the station to bring it in line with western standards
Temelin, some 100 km south of Prague, will be equipped with two Soviet-designed 1000 megawatt reactors along with a control system supplied by U.S.-based Westinghouse Electric Corp.
Enviromentalists from the Czech Republic and neighbouring Austria have campaigned against completion of the plant, saying it is dangerous, expensive and unnecessary.
CEZ has said the plant will allow it to close down some polluting coal-burning power plants in the north of the Czech Republic.
